topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: The rain slicks the streets like old secrets, pooling in the gutters, same as the ones I've seen down a dozen mirrors. Two siblings, huh? Inherit a house, they do. Grandmother's place, she’s gone, and now they're standing in the middle of what used to be her life, trying to figure out what to do with the pieces. One's got the shine in their eye, the kind that says they're already seeing the money. The other, they're looking around, like they can still feel her ghost in the air, the weight of the past pressing down. In this business, I've seen it all. The way family ties can fray under the pressure of a house full of memories and unspoken words. I've got a hunch this isn’t going to be a simple case of dividing the spoils. Not with those looks passing between them. Not in this city.
